question: How do I register for courses for the upcoming semester?
answer: Course registration opens one week before the semester starts via the AASTU Student Information Portal (SIMS). Log in using your student ID and password, navigate to 'Course Registration', select your required core courses and electives recommended by your academic advisor, and click 'Submit for Advisor Approval'. Once your advisor approves, your registration slip is generated automatically.

question: What is the deadline and procedure for adding or dropping a course?
answer: The add/drop period lasts for the first two weeks of the academic semester. You must fill out the Add/Drop Slip available on the student portal or at the Registrar Office, secure the signatures of both course instructors and your department chair, and submit the physical form or finalized digital request before 5:00 PM on Friday of the second week. Late requests incur administrative penalties.

question: How do I replace a lost student ID card?
answer: If you lose your student ID card, report it to the Campus Security Office in Administration Building Block 1 to obtain a loss verification letter. Pay the 150 ETB replacement fee at the Finance Cashier Office or via Telebirr (AASTU Merchant Code), then bring the receipt and police letter to the Registrar Records Window to receive a newly printed student badge within 24 hours.

question: How does the AASTU grading system work and what is considered academic probation?
answer: AASTU operates on a standard 4.00 Grade Point Average (GPA) scale: A+ and A are 4.0, A- is 3.75, B+ is 3.5, B is 3.0, B- is 2.75, C+ is 2.5, C is 2.0, D is 1.0, and F is 0.0. A cumulative GPA (CGPA) or semester GPA (SGPA) below 2.00 places an undergraduate student on Academic Probation. Two consecutive probation semesters lead to academic dismissal or repetition depending on department policy.
tags: grading scale, GPA, CGPA, probation, dismissal

question: How do I appeal an exam grade if I suspect an evaluation error?
answer: Grade appeals must be formally lodged within 5 business days after grades are officially posted on the portal. Complete the Grade Re-evaluation Form at your Department Office and attach evidence such as returned midterm assessments or project logs. A formal review committee comprising the department head and an independent faculty member will review your exam script with the instructor within 10 working days.
tags: grade appeal, exam dispute, re-evaluation, academic affairs

question: How can I request an official academic transcript or letter of enrollment?
answer: Official transcripts and student verification letters can be ordered through the Registrar self-service portal or at Window 3 of the Central Registrar. Ensure you have settled all campus clearances (library books, laboratory equipment, tuition/cost sharing). Standard processing takes 3 working days, and expedited delivery for scholarship applications takes 24 hours with an official request letter.

question: How do I connect to the AASTU high-speed campus Wi-Fi network?
answer: Connect your laptop or smartphone to the 'AASTU-Student' SSID. When prompted, use your university institutional email address (e.g. firstname.lastname@aastu.edu.et) as the username and your SIMS portal password. If certificate verification appears on Android or iOS, select 'Trust on First Use' or choose 'Do not validate' for the domain. If connection fails, visit the ICT Helpdesk in Block 42, Ground Floor.

question: I forgot my student portal password. How do I reset it?
answer: To reset your password, visit the portal login page and click 'Forgot Password'. Enter your registered student ID number or your official student email address. A password reset link valid for 15 minutes will be sent to your inbox. Alternatively, visit the ICT Directorate Helpdesk in Block 42 with your physical student ID for an instant identity verification and password reset.
tags: password reset, forgot password, portal, login, credentials

question: How do I activate and access my official AASTU Google Workspace student email?
answer: New students receive an email account during freshman orientation. Go to gmail.com and sign in with 'firstname.lastname@aastu.edu.et'. Your default temporary password is 'Aastu@' followed by the last 4 digits of your student ID. You will be prompted to set a new strong password with 2-factor authentication enabled on your mobile device.

question: What are the central library opening hours and how do I borrow physical textbooks?
answer: The AASTU Central Library is open Monday through Friday from 8:00 AM to 10:00 PM, and Saturdays & Sundays from 8:30 AM to 6:00 PM. During final exam weeks, reading halls operate on a 24/7 schedule. To borrow books, present your student barcode at the circulation desk on the 1st floor. Undergraduate students may borrow up to 3 books for a duration of 14 days, renewable once online.

question: How do I access IEEE Xplore, ScienceDirect, and digital research journals off-campus?
answer: Access digital research databases via the AASTU Institutional Repository and Digital Library page (library.aastu.edu.et). When off-campus, configure the AASTU EZproxy or OpenVPN client provided by ICT. Enter your university credentials to gain complimentary proxy access to IEEE Xplore, SpringerLink, ScienceDirect, and ACM Digital Library research papers.

question: How does dormitory allocation work and how do I request maintenance?
answer: Dormitory rooms are allocated at the beginning of each academic year based on student gender, disability accommodations, and year of study. Freshman and senior students receive priority placement. For room maintenance (plumbing, lighting, or bed issues), submit a maintenance ticket via the Dorm Proctor's Office on the ground floor of your respective residential block.

question: What are the student cafeteria meal times and dietary provisions?
answer: The main student dining hall serves breakfast from 6:30 AM to 8:30 AM, lunch from 11:30 AM to 1:30 PM, and dinner from 6:00 PM to 8:00 PM. AASTU dining provides separate meal service lines for fasting and non-fasting dietary schedules throughout the academic term. Present your electronic meal voucher card at the entry turnstile.

question: Where is the student clinic located and what medical services are free?
answer: The AASTU Health Center is located near Dormitory Block 18 and is open 24/7 for acute medical care and first aid. Basic consultations, prescribed generic medications, emergency ambulance transfers to Black Lion (Tikur Anbessa) or Zewditu Hospital, and mental health counseling are free of charge for all enrolled students carrying a valid student badge.

question: How do I apply for mandatory 4th-year university engineering internships?
answer: The Industry Linkage Office coordinates mandatory 4th-year semester internships with corporate partners across Ethiopia (including Ethio Telecom, Ethiopian Airlines, INSA, and industrial parks). In the first month of Year 4 Semester 1, submit your preferred host companies and your updated resume through the internship portal. Official placement letters are issued by December.

question: What is higher education cost-sharing and when do I sign my contract?
answer: Cost-sharing covers student tuition, lodging, and food subsidies funded by the Ethiopian government. Every government-sponsored undergraduate must sign the annual cost-sharing contractual commitment during the first month of enrollment at the Cost Sharing Office. Repayment begins after graduation once you gain formal employment with an official tax identification number (TIN).
